blocks.heading: Ranthambore Travel Guide
blocks.intro: Carefully curated practical guides prepared by our naturalists to help you prepare for an unforgettable tiger safari.

items.title: Best Time to Visit Ranthambore: Month-by-Month Guide
items.text: From misty winter mornings (Nov-Feb) to hot summer months (Apr-Jun) when tigers frequent waterholes, understand seasonal sighting patterns.

items.title: Essential Safari Packing List: What to Wear in the Jungle
items.text: Why earthy greens, browns, and khakis matter, essential winter layers for open Gypsy drives, dust protection, and camera beanbags.

items.title: How to Reach Ranthambore: Train, Road & Flight Options
items.text: Direct express trains to Sawai Madhopur (SWM), flight connections via Jaipur (JAI), and the new Delhi-Mumbai Expressway route.

blocks.heading: Best Time to Visit Ranthambore
blocks.intro: Each season offers unique wildlife sightings, photography light, and landscape moods.

items.title: October to November
items.text: The park reopens with vibrant green foliage, waterfalls in ravines, and high lake water levels. Excellent for landscape photography and birding.

items.title: December to February
items.text: Chilly morning safaris requiring warm fleece jackets. Tigers frequently bask in open grasslands, ruins, and sunny dirt tracks.

items.title: March to April
items.text: Palash trees (Flame of the Forest) burst into orange blossoms. As foliage thins, animal visibility across ravines and lakes increases.

items.title: May to June
items.text: Water sources dry up, concentrating tigers near Padam, Rajbagh, and Malik Talao lakes. Unmatched predator action and photography opportunities.

blocks.heading: Safari Packing & Dress Code Essentials
blocks.intro: Blend into the wilderness and stay comfortable on open 4x4 Gypsy drives

groups.title: Clothing Colors
items: Earthy tones (Khaki, Olive Green, Muted Brown). Avoid bright red, neon, or stark white.

groups.title: Weather Gear
items: Heavy fleece jackets for winter mornings; light breathable cottons, sun hat & shades for summer.

groups.title: Dust Protection
items: Bandana / scarf / buff to cover nose & mouth from dirt tracks; dust cover sleeve for camera lens.

groups.title: Optics & Tech
items: Binoculars (8x42 or 10x42), telephoto lens (100-400mm or 70-200mm), extra memory cards and batteries.

groups.title: Personal Care
items: High SPF sunscreen, mosquito repellent, lip balm, rehydration electrolytes (ORS), and personal medicines.

groups.title: Govt. Documents
items: Original Government Photo ID (exact proof provided during online booking) is 100% mandatory.

blocks.heading: Wildlife Photography Masterclass Tips
blocks.intro: Capturing Royal Bengal Tigers in dense dry deciduous scrub

items.title: Lens Recommendation
items.text: A versatile 100-400mm or 150-600mm telephoto zoom is ideal. Tigers frequently cross right in front of the vehicle or walk across lake edges 80m away.

items.title: Bean Bag Stabilization
items.text: Tripods are prohibited inside safari vehicles. Bring an unfilled bean bag to rest your telephoto lens smoothly on the Gypsy safety rail.

items.title: Shutter Speed & Shaded Light
items.text: Keep shutter speeds above 1/1000s for moving animals. Raise ISO to 1600–3200 under dense Dhok canopy and early morning low-light shifts.

blocks.heading: Dos & Don'ts in the Tiger Reserve

groups.title: Dos (Must Follow)
items: Always follow the instructions of your assigned forest naturalist guide.
Remain seated inside the vehicle at all times; disembarking is strictly forbidden.
Keep your voice at a low whisper when an animal or tiger is sighted.
Carry drinking water, hat, and sunglasses for open-top sun exposure.

groups.title: Don'ts (Strictly Prohibited)
items: Do NOT litter or throw plastic bottles/wrappers inside the national park.
Do NOT use camera flash or make loud noises to provoke wildlife.
Do NOT play music, blow horns, or carry pets into the reserve.
Do NOT smoke or ignite fires anywhere within the protected forest area.
